subject: Urgent: Save request for Nuvista subscription — proposed term reset, credit & SLA add-on
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Save request for Nuvista subscription — propose term reset & SLA add-on

Team,

Quick context: Nuvista Health (annual subscription, ~$1.2M ARR) notified us yesterday that their procurement lead is pulling the renewal because two internal stakeholders are pushing for a different vendor over price and a short historical outage last quarter. They want an answer by EOD Jun 5 or they will reprocure.

Current ask from customer (via their CSM): extend the contract term start (term reset) to today for 12 months, add a 99.9% uptime SLA with credits, and a one‑time retention credit in the range of $80–120k. They also asked if we can discount next year by 10–20% — they say budget pressure is the main driver.

Proposed concession package for approval:
- One-time credit: $50,000 (applied to upcoming invoice)
- Term reset: shift anniversary to 6/1/2026 for a new 12‑month term (requires contract amendment)
- SLA add-on: 99.9% uptime with standard SLA credit table for 12 months
- Marketing ask denied (customer asked for co-marketing; recommend decline)

Rationale: account strategic (healthcare partner), upsell pipeline attached to platform integrations, risk of >$1M churn. Finance margin impact (approx): ~6% net impact in year 1 if we do $50k credit + SLA. Alternate ask from AM: they might accept a larger credit in lieu of term reset.

Attachments: Nuvista_Retention_Scenarios.pdf, Nuvista_contract_redline.pdf (redlines on term reset).

Request: Exec signoff needed on the above concession package (term reset + $50k credit + SLA add-on). If approved, Legal & Finance will scope amendments and we will get DocuSign. I need a response by EOD Mon Jun 1 to have time to negotiate their counter.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Save request for Nuvista subscription — propose term reset & SLA add-on

Hannah — thanks for the summary. A few quick questions before I can sign off:
1) Can you confirm expected ARR retention vs. churn probability if we do nothing? (ballpark is fine)
2) Who owns the SLA implementation/ops risk here — Product or the Dedicated team? I need a note on operational exposure for 99.9% SLA.
3) Finance: please confirm impact to gross margin and whether this can be handled as a one-time credit vs. discount to list.

If margin hit is >8% and ops exposure is material, I want to consider a middle option: $75k credit + SLA limited to platform (not infra) or a 9‑month term reset.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
COO, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Save request for Nuvista subscription — propose term reset & SLA add-on

Adding AM color — I spoke with Liz (procurement) and Michael (CTO). Their escalations:
- Primary driver is procurement push for lower supplier TCO (they have a preferred vendor with a lower list).
- Secondary is last quarter's 6hr availability incident (we already applied an incident credit but they want stronger guarantees).

Customer willingness (direct):
- Credit request: originally asked for $120k; they explicitly said $80k would be satisfactory.
- Term reset: they prefer full 12 months reset to avoid a mid-contract switch; see redline.
- SLA: they will accept platform-only 99.9% if we cap infra-dependent exclusions.

Concession alternatives I recommend for approval (ranked):
A) Approve $50k credit + 12m term reset + platform 99.9% SLA add-on (fastest to close).
B) Approve $80k credit + no term reset + platform 99.9% SLA + stronger support hours.
C) Approve $120k credit (worst case) + 12m term reset if they push.

HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/HS-789204 — there are notes from Procurement. I uploaded an MAAP with ARR scenarios: Nuvista_MAAP.xlsx.

Marissa
Account Manager — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Save request for Nuvista subscription — propose term reset & SLA add-on

Folks — quick legal view:
- Term reset is non-standard; requires amendment and approval from our commercial leadership (signature authority). It also changes renewal cadence and could set precedent.
- SLA add-on is doable but needs Product sign-off for measurable SLOs and an implementation acceptance criteria. Product will want to limit infra exclusions (we can specify platform-level SLOs only).
- One-time credits are contractually simpler and less precedent-setting than hard discounts or term resets.

Attached: Nuvista_contract_redline.pdf with suggested language for a 12-month reset + credit application. If Execs approve a credit + SLA approach, we can draft and send to the customer within 48 hours.

Neha
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
From: Liz Carter <liz.carter@nuvistahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@nuvistahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Save request for Nuvista subscription — proposed term reset, credit & SLA add-on

Hannah/Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround. We want to avoid a full RFP; procurement has a June 7 internal deadline to give direction to Finance. Short summary of our preferences: 1) term reset preferred, 2) SLA is required (platform-only acceptable), 3) $80k credit would put us over the line.

If Redwood can do $80k + platform 99.9% SLA + a signed amendment by Jun 5, we can push for approval on our end. If you need to come down on credit, $60k is our minimum acceptable.

Liz Carter
Director, Procurement — Nuvista Health
liz.carter@nuvistahealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Save request for Nuvista subscription — proposed term reset & SLA add-on

Team — after reviewing options and margin impact, I will approve the following conditional package to close this renewal:
- One-time credit: $60,000 (to be applied to upcoming invoice)
- SLA add-on: platform 99.9% uptime for 12 months (Legal to finalize SLO language with Product)
- Term reset: NO. We will not reset the contract anniversary; instead we will offer a 12-month addendum that preserves original renewal cadence (reduces precedent risk).

Conditions:
- Finance to confirm P&L treatment and that the credit can be booked as a one-time contra-revenue item.
- Legal to finalize amendment language and confirm no additional indemnity or expanded liability.
- Sales to get a signed amendment by Jun 5 from Nuvista.

This is capped approval — do not exceed $60k credit or make changes to liability language. If customer won't sign to these terms, escalate back to me with clear alternatives.

Vivek Kulkarni
COO, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jun 03, 2026 at 09:12 AM PDT Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Noted — I'll coordinate Legal & Finance and push for signature. Will report back with the signed amendment or next steps.

> Hannah
